about: One feature per wiring ticket in docs/WIRING.md, plus WA (adapter hardening) and WC (contract write cases). Checks restate what the ticket's spec in tests/e2e/ asserts. Every ticket also keeps auth.spec.ts, w0 and the earlier tickets' specs green, plus npm run typecheck and npm run test:contract. src/ui/api/index.js is in SHARED_TOUCHES (kit/project.env): each ticket uncomments only its own lines under its own // Wn header, so parallel tickets merge cleanly. New integration tests go in their own file (tests/integration/wN-*.test.ts), never in a shared one. Only WC edits tests/contract/contract.test.ts: if a ticket needs a new contract case, say so under notes in the report.

features.title: Sign-in wired into the screens (WIRING Step 1), dashboard live
checks: src/ui/api/index.js is in the Step 2 form, with every area on its own line under a ticket header, in this order: // W0 'dashboard'; // W1 'taxonomy' 'fast'; // W2 'families' 'invites'; // W3 'messages' 'notifications'; // W4 'books' 'content'; // W5 'assignments'; // W6 'scheduling'; // W7 'reports' 'ai'. Only 'dashboard' is uncommented, so liveAreas() in tests/e2e/support/live.ts is exactly { dashboard } and the w0 spec runs.

Both group layouts pass session.user into <AppRoot user={…}>. AppRoot takes the role from user.role (not the URL) and the text size from user.textSize, and calls setSessionUser(user.id) while any area is on the mock.

The shell (ShellContext.jsx) takes the signed-in user from what AppRoot passes in, never from the mock's auth(), so a parent who isn't in the mock's seed (a new sign-up) gets a working shell, not a TypeError.
Each parent sees their own family: signed in as Grace, /parent/home shows Noah and not Mateo; as Ana, the 'Choose a child' tablist shows Mateo and Lucia (phone width too).
The account panel shows the signed-in email (grace.kim@example.com) and has no 'Demo account' radiogroup.
Choosing 'Larger' text sets #mm-root data-text to XLARGE, saves User.textSize = XLARGE, and survives a reload (router.refresh() after the save).
'Sign out' calls signOutNow() from src/app/(auth)/sign-in/actions.ts and lands on /sign-in; /parent/home afterwards redirects to /sign-in (phone width too).
A preview parent (Tom, status PREVIEW) sees 'Enter your invite code' and an 'Invite code' field (InviteCodeForm) until they redeem a code.

When session.user.mustChangePassword is true, the parent is asked for a new password before anything else; it calls families.changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword }) with the temporary password as currentPassword, and goes to /sign-in if the result has signInAgain: true. The account panel has a 'Change password' row that uses the same call. Covered by a new tests/e2e/change-password.spec.ts that uses requiresSignInWired().
npm run build:e2e && npm run test:e2e -- w0 auth change-password passes; npm run test:contract is green.
hints: families stays on the mock until W2, so account-level calls (families.setTextSize, families.changePassword) go to the real server directly via live.families from src/ui/api/live.js, not through api.families.

features.title: Live adapter: plain errors instead of crashes, keep data on a failed refetch
checks: asWrite in src/ui/api/live.js catches a thrown call (network drop, a redirect after the session ended) and returns { ok: false, error: 'We couldn’t reach the server. Check your connection and try again.', code: 'NETWORK' }. There's no unhandled rejection, and the screen's usual error toast shows the message.
When the thrown error is Next's 'Failed to find Server Action' (the app was redeployed under an open tab), the message is 'The app was just updated. Reload the page to keep going.' with code 'STALE'.
asRead throws the same plain messages as an Error with .code ('NETWORK' or 'STALE'), so reads and writes fail the same way.

useQuery in src/ui/api/live-hooks.js keeps the last good data when a refetch fails and exposes the error as state.error. It throws to the error boundary only when there's no data yet, so one failed background refetch (a paused parent's badges getting NOT_ACTIVE, say) never blanks the app.
content.uploadFile passes the caller's mimeType through when file.type is empty (some phones send blank or HEIC types; AnswerSheet.jsx sends f.type || 'image/jpeg').
tests/live-adapter.test.ts (unit project: vitest run --project unit) covers each check above with a fake server function. npm run typecheck and npm run test:contract stay green.
hints: src/lib/upload-client.ts is Zero's path, so this PR is held for Zero. Keep the change to taking an optional mimeType.
Don't change what the screens read: a successful read still returns r.data, and a write still returns the { ok, data | error, code } result.

features.title: Invite codes can't be brute-forced across accounts
checks: Every failed redeemInvite adds a row to a new RedeemFailure table (userId, at; indexed on at; userId references User with onDelete: Cascade), made by a committed migration (npx prisma migrate dev --name redeem-failures).
A refusal while locked, whether by the global limit or the per-account one, adds no RedeemFailure row, so a locked account can't keep the global count up.

Once there are more than GLOBAL_REDEEM_FAILURES_PER_HOUR (30, a constant in src/server/invites.ts) failures in the last hour across all accounts, every redeem returns code LOCKED with 'Too many tries right now. Try again in an hour, or ask Vienne to check the code.', a correct code included.
Vienne gets one alert when the limit is first reached in an hour, sent after the transaction commits (lib/notify.ts), never one per try.
The per-account limit (MAX_FAILURES, LOCK_MS) and the MM-XXXX code shape stay as they are; the w2 spec checks the shape.

Tests in tests/integration/s5-redeem.test.ts: the 31st failure in an hour locks every account, an hour later redeeming works again, and the alert goes out once. The w2 spec and npm run test:contract stay green.
hints: Why: 32^4 ≈ 1.05M codes, free accounts and a per-account lock only, so 1,000 accounts could try 3M+ codes in a code's 14 days (VALID_DAYS).
Notification.type is a String, so the alert needs no enum change. Held for Zero (prisma, src/server).

features.title: Redeem limits hold under parallel tries; old failure rows are cleaned up
checks: redeemInvite reads the account's redeemFailures and redeemLockedUntil again inside the advisory-lock transaction, so MAX_FAILURES wrong codes sent at once from one account lock it, and the next try gets LOCKED. (Before, each parallel try counted from the same stale value.)

A right code is checked against GLOBAL_REDEEM_FAILURES_PER_HOUR under the same advisory lock before it's claimed. Past the limit it gets the same LOCKED message as a wrong code, until the hour passes, as S5 says (every redeem returns LOCKED). The code isn't used up.
cleanUp in src/lib/jobs.ts (the daily job) deletes RedeemFailure rows older than a day and returns how many (redeemFailures). Rows from the last hour still count toward the limit.

Tests in tests/integration/s5b-redeem.test.ts: parallel wrong codes from one account (separate calls in Promise.all, never on tx), a right code past the global limit, and the cleanup. tests/integration/s5-redeem.test.ts, the w2 spec and npm run test:contract stay green.
hints: Held for Zero (src/server, src/lib).
MAX_FAILURES, LOCK_MS, GLOBAL_REDEEM_FAILURES_PER_HOUR and the alert to Vienne don't change. Take the same lock the failure path takes (pg_advisory_xact_lock(7300530001)).
Check 1 is Zero's (a race older than S5). Check 2 is from Rigg's S5 review (S5's global pre-check runs outside the lock).

features.title: Production audit, security (Zero): guards, leaks, files, limits, migrations, dependencies
checks: tests/integration/p-sec.test.ts calls every export of every src/server/*.ts signed out and gets UNAUTHENTICATED, except the exports it lists as public, each with its reason. A new export without a guard fails CI. Every export also parse()s its input with zod before any lookup: a wrong-typed input gets INVALID, not a crash.

features.title: Production audit, ops (Atlas): env check, cron secret, private Blob, backups, spend caps, rollback
checks: Env check: productionProblems (src/lib/env-check.ts) reports nothing for the production environment's variable names (values are never printed or pasted), and DEMO_MODE isn't set in any Vercel environment.

Cron: /api/cron/daily refuses a request without CRON_SECRET, and the job runs once a day in production. vercel.json still uses legacy `crons`: the report decides whether to move it to Vercel Schedules (`schedules`), with the reason. If it moves, the route's secret check still holds.
Blob: the store is private. A stored file's raw Blob URL doesn't open without a token, and files reach people only through /api/files.
Neon: the point-in-time restore window is on, and one restore into a new branch (never over main) is rehearsed and timed in docs/DEPLOY.md.
Spend caps: a Vercel spend limit, the Neon plan's limit and a Claude Console limit are set, and AI_DAILY_LIMIT (src/lib/ai/prompts.ts) is noted in docs/COSTS.md beside them.
Rollback: an instant rollback to the previous deployment is rehearsed on a preview, not production, and the steps are in docs/DEPLOY.md.
hints: Run by its owner, not a lane (role audit). The owner works on f/P-ops in .wt/ and runs kit/plan.py set P-ops doing when it starts. The audit writes tests, docs and its report. A finding that needs app code becomes an S ticket for the lanes, listed in the report; it isn't fixed in the audit PR.
Production setup (Vercel Pro, Neon, Blob, Google OAuth on Vienne's account) waits until W8, and Javaris does every click. Atlas prepares the steps and checks the result.
Held for Axis (docs): Axis merges Atlas's audit PR.

features.title: Production audit, independent review (OSA) of P-sec, P-product and P-ops
checks: OSA reads the three audit reports and the app, not the auditors' conclusions, and lists anything they missed. Each finding becomes an S ticket, or a Before launch item for Javaris.
Launch waits until every S ticket from the audit has merged and P-review says so.
hints: OSA sets the review's scope. This ticket only puts it on the board, after the three audits.
